faq.q: What do I do in the look step?
faq.a: Look carefully at the word. Notice its shape, the tall letters, and any tricky bit you cannot hear.
asks: Tell me about the look step

faq.q: Why do I cover the word?
faq.a: Covering it makes your brain remember the word on its own. That is how the spelling moves into your memory.

faq.q: What if I get the spelling wrong?
faq.a: That is part of learning! Look at the bit you missed, then go round the five steps again. Every try makes it stronger.

faq.q: How many spellings should I learn at once?
faq.a: Start with just three to five words. A little practice every day works better than lots in one go. A teacher or grown-up can test you.

faq.q: How can I make spelling practice more fun?
faq.a: Write in sand, with chalk, with a finger on the table, or in rainbow colours. Moving and saying together helps words stick.
